Kimberly —

Thanks again for the intro. Were moving toward a committed Redwood Dedicated purchase and need a short modelling exercise so procurement can align on a commit tier. Quick context and asks below.

Summary:
- Production app will be primarily user-facing chat + summarization.
- Expected steady-state: ~120 tokens/sec (user mix), daily average ~10M tokens/day.
- Peak bursts: up to ~800 tokens/sec (short bursts, <15 minutes).
- Model mix: primarily 13B for chat (est. ~90%), occasional 70B for long summarization jobs (~10%).
- SLOs: p99 latency target for generation token-level budget ~250ms; p50 ~80ms.

Ask: can you map tokens/sec -> GPUs (H100) for our model mix and show headroom scenarios (1.2x, 2x, 3x over peak)? Procurement wants the recommended committed GPUs + suggested burst capacity. Attached is our sampled traffic CSV and a short SLO doc.

Attachments: [Attachment: citrine_observed_traffic.csv (csv)], [Attachment: slo_and_latency_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

Happy to jump on a short call — available Wed/Thu afternoons PT.

Citrine AI

Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing request and observed traffic — initial tokens/sec sims

Celine / Kimberly —

I ran a quick set of baseline throughput estimates using our internal perf numbers (H100, kernel-optimized runtime) and the model mix you described. Assumptions: 4-bit quantization allowed for 13B (recommended for cost), 70B run in fp16 for quality. Context length 2048, average generation length 64 tokens per request for chat flows.

Per-GPU (H100) sustained generation throughput (tokens/sec):
- redwood-13b (4-bit): ~720 tps per GPU
- redwood-70b (fp16): ~180 tps per GPU

Scenarios (target instantaneous peak = 800 tps):
- Model split: 90% 13B (720 tps of demand), 10% 70B (80 tps of demand).
- Capacity needed (raw): 13B side -> 1 GPU (720/720 = 1); 70B side -> 1 GPU (80/180 = 0.45 -> 1).

But raw math ignores SLO headroom, concurrency spikes, and KV caching behavior. Recommendations weve used for similar deals:
- Safety factor 1.5x for predictable p95 traffic
- Safety factor 2.5-3x for p99/operational headroom depending on business-criticality

Quick recommended commitments (instantaneous peak = 800 tps):
- Conservative (1.5x headroom): reserve 3 GPUs (2x 13B-capable, 1x 70B-capable) + 1 burst GPU.
- Aggressive (3x headroom / p99): reserve 5 GPUs + 2 burst GPUs.

I attached a short workbook with the per-GPU numbers and an adjustable slider to test percent long-form workload and burst multipliers.

Attachments: [Attachment: r_mehta_tps_runbook.xlsx (xlsx)]

Ill prepare a commit-tier suggestion once Celine confirms the smoothing window to size for (1-min p99 vs. 5-min average).

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Principal SRE — Serving Performance, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, Celine Park <celine@citrine.ai>, rohan.mehta@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing request — commit recommendation and headroom math

Folks —

I consolidated the numbers and produced a short recommendation for procurement. Im keeping the math explicit so procurement can trace commitments back to traffic assumptions.

Inputs (confirmed):
- Peak instantaneous observed: 850 tps (short spike); sustained marketing event peak used for sizing: 600 tps
- Model mix: 90% 13B, 10% 70B
- Per-GPU throughput (H100): 13B (4-bit) = 720 tps; 70B (fp16) = 180 tps
- SLO window: 1-min p99

Effective demand breakdown at 600 tps sustained:
- 13B portion = 540 tps -> requires 540/720 = 0.75 GPUs (round up to 1)
- 70B portion = 60 tps -> requires 60/180 = 0.33 GPUs (round up to 1)

Sizing guidelines we recommend for Dedicated commits:
- Minimal commit (covers sustained peak 600 tps, ~1-min p99 with 2x safety): reserve 4 H100 GPUs. Rationale: round-up per model, then apply 2x safety margin to address request bursts and concurrent healthy headroom (1+1 -> 2 -> *2 = 4).
- Preferred commit (predictable for marketing events and 3x headroom for p99): reserve 6 H100 GPUs, with 2 additional burst GPUs on on-demand to cover 850 tps short spikes. This maps to a 6-GPU commit that gives room for 3x headroom without immediate scaling events.

Operational notes / recommended policies:
- Autoscaler: keep burst pool (on-demand) for short spikes above commit; policy: scale-up immediate for 1-2 GPUs if p99 breached, scale gradually for sustained >10 minutes.
- Model placement: pin 2 GPUs as mixed-model worker nodes (can run 13B and 70B via runtime routing) to increase utilization. Avoid strict one-model-per-GPU unless 70B traffic rises >30%.
- Canary & rollout: start with 3 reserved GPUs as a warmup (test routing and KV cache benefits) before ramping to full commit. Can parallelize with procurement to accelerate.

Recommendation for procurement box to sign:
- Option A (baseline): 4x H100 reserved, 12-month term, with 2x burst credits for on-demand (covers most marketing events).
- Option B (recommended): 6x H100 reserved, 12-month term, with 4x burst credits for on-demand. Option B reduces throttle risk for p99-sensitive features and provides runway for growth.

I attached a consolidated sizing spreadsheet with the spreadsheets for the different multipliers and a one-page summary you can share with procurement.

Attachments: [Attachment: commit_sizing_consolidated.xlsx (xlsx)]

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Capacity & Reliability, Redwood Inference
